slides.title: The SAT gives you a ==cheat code== — most students never open it
Graph both sides of any equation
slides.body: Solving for x? Type the left side as one graph and the right side as another. The x-value where they cross *is* the answer, because two graphs meet exactly where the two sides are equal. Works on linear, quadratic, exponential — anything with one variable.

slides.title: Quadratics, decoded on sight
slides.body: Type the quadratic in and Desmos marks the zeros and the vertex as gray points — click them to see the values. "How many solutions?" becomes counting where the parabola crosses the x-axis. No discriminant, no factoring, no formula.

slides.title: Systems in seconds
slides.body: Type both equations and click the intersection point — that ordered pair is the solution. Parallel lines that never touch? That's what "no solution" looks like. The graph answers the question before the algebra would have started.
